items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: Well, I used to play with my brother a lot. I was standing together, and he played a little piano.

ctx.x: Well, he didn't play but the melody. You weren't making many variations then? No. But when did you start to do that? Well, I guess we practiced.

Just used to practice hard, you know. Every time I hear somebody make a vary, I'd whistle it until I get home, grab my horn, feel for it on my horn. Did you have a play along? I didn't think it would sound good to me. I did. Mm-hmm. Did you ever play along with anybody else, with records or with a piano, or any of those times, to study? Well, I used to play with my brother a lot. I was standing together, and he played a little piano. Mm-hmm. I ain't surprised it was him. Yeah. Yeah.

Yeah. Was there any special clarinet players that you used to hear and get ideas from? You know, things that you'd whistle and then play there? Well, I think I like a little bit from the Sender County guys. Yeah. On the records? Yeah.
